name: Journalist, PR Specialist and Communicator
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Two occupations, one degree family, opposite directions. Journalists: 47,100 jobs, 3,400 openings a year, $62,200, projected to DECLINE 6%. Public relations specialists: 314,500 jobs, 23,000 openings, $74,750, growing. ⚠⚠ PR is nearly SEVEN times the occupation, pays $12,550 more and has nearly seven times the openings — and Florida trains eight communication graduates for every journalism one.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ NOTHING HERE IS LICENSED AND NO MAJOR IS REQUIRED. BLS gives a bachelor's as the typical entry for both journalists and public relations specialists, but no state licence, no registry and no examination exists in either. The portfolio — clips, campaigns, work people can read — is the credential. ⚠⚠⚠ AND THE REASON JOURNALISM IS SHRINKING IS NOT TECHNOLOGY IN THE SENSE EVERYONE ASSUMES. BLS attributes the projected 6% decline to DECLINING ADVERTISING REVENUE in radio, newspapers and television, and to CONSOLIDATION of news organisations reducing staffing — with increased demand for online news content partially offsetting it. ⚠ It does not name artificial intelligence. That matters, because the contraction is a business-model problem that began well before generative tools existed, and it will not reverse if the tools improve. ⚠⚠ What follows practically: the reporting and verification training is excellent and it travels, but plan the exits from the first year rather than the fourth. 17% of journalists are self-employed, which in this field usually means freelancing into a shrinking market rather than choosing independence. ⚠ The credential that does get named on the PR side is the APR, offered by the Public Relations Society of America, which requires professional experience rather than a degree — a mid-career mark, not a way in.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ Same degree family, opposite directions

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2025–35
⚠⚠ News analyst, reporter, journalist27-3023$62,200⚠ 47,100⚠ 3,400⚠⚠⚠ −6%
✅ Public relations specialist27-3031✅ $74,750✅ 314,500✅ 23,000+2%

⚠⚠⚠ Public relations is nearly seven times the occupation, pays $12,550 more, and has nearly seven times the annual openings. Both take a bachelor's, neither is licensed, and the writing skills overlap almost completely.

⚠⚠ Florida's training follows the jobs, not the romance: 292 journalism bachelor's a year against roughly 2,350 in communication, public relations and advertising. Eight communication graduates for every journalism one.

⚠⚠⚠ Why journalism is shrinking, in BLS's own account

The handbook attributes the projected 6% decline to:

  • declining advertising revenue in radio, newspapers and television;
  • consolidation of news organisations, which reduces staffing;
  • the difficulty traditional advertising models face as online publishing expands.

It adds that increased demand for online news content may partially offset some job losses.

⚠⚠⚠ Note what is NOT in that list: artificial intelligence. This site now covers four other creative and information occupations where BLS does discuss automation — graphic design (“reduce the need for these workers”), web development (“soften the employment growth”), medical records (no dampening claim) and film editing (no AI claim, robotic cameras instead). Journalism's contraction is a BUSINESS-MODEL problem, and it began well before generative tools existed.

⚠⚠ That distinction is practical rather than academic. A decline caused by tooling might reverse or plateau as the tooling matures. A decline caused by advertising revenue leaving an industry does not reverse because the software gets better.

⚠⚠ The honest position on studying journalism

This page is not telling you not to. Reporting and verification is the best writing training in this family: sourcing, interviewing, structure under deadline, and the habit of checking. It travels into every occupation on this page and several elsewhere on this site.

⚠⚠⚠ What it is telling you is to plan the exits in your first year rather than your fourth, because 3,400 national openings a year against 292 Florida graduates in one state is a market you should enter deliberately and not by default.

⚠ And 17% of journalists are self-employed — which in a contracting field usually means freelancing into it rather than choosing independence. Read that number differently from the 35% in film or the 63% in animation.

⚠⚠ Where a communication degree actually goes

Destination2025 medianOpenings/yr
✅✅ Marketing manager✅ $166,79034,300
Training and development specialist$69,280✅ 43,900
Public relations specialist$74,75023,000
Market research analyst / marketing specialist$78,760✅ 87,200
⚠ Journalist$62,200⚠ 3,400

⚠⚠⚠ Census microdata puts COMMUNICATIONS second among the undergraduate fields held by marketing managers, at 88,800 people — behind business at 175,070 and ahead of social sciences. That is an evidenced route to a $166,790 median from this degree family, and almost nobody points at it.

⚠ The numbering, which is unsettled in two places

PairCarriersOverlap
JOU1100 Basic Reporting7 — ALL state colleges⚠ none
JOU2100 Journalistic Writing and Reporting8 — 3 state colleges, 5 universities
ADV3300 Media Planning4 universities⚠ none
ADV4300 Media Planning4 different universities

⚠ Both pairs are consistent in level within themselves, so no baccalaureate credit is at risk. The cost is transfer matching — an evaluator comparing ADV3300 against ADV4300 sees two numbers and one course. Send the syllabus.

⚠⚠ And two documented divergences in this family are worth knowing before you register. PUR3000 is Principles of Public Relations at UF and FGCU — the general introduction with the history of the profession, ethics and the PR process — while UWF teaches Introduction to Public Affairs, which is government and nonprofit policy communication. Public affairs is a subfield of PR, so a UWF student misses PR history, media relations and campaigns entirely. And JOU4306 is Critical Journalism statewide, but UWF teaches arts criticism on it and UF teaches ADVANCED DATA JOURNALISM IN R — the prerequisite is the tell: gated on a data course means the data version.

Necessary skills

  • Reporting. Finding out things people would rather you did not, and checking them. The durable skill in this entire family.
  • Writing to structure under a deadline, which is a craft and not a talent.
  • Interviewing — the same skill a PR practitioner, a market researcher and a UX designer all need.
  • Media law and ethics: defamation, privacy, access, source protection.
  • Measurement, on the PR side especially. The practitioners who can prove an effect get the budget.
  • Multi-channel production — audio, video, social, newsletter. Nobody in this family writes only prose any more.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Take the journalism training and plan the exit. The reporting education is excellent and it is the best writing schooling in this family — but 3,400 national openings a year in a 6% decline is a market to enter with open eyes.

⚠⚠ Look hard at the marketing ladder. Census data puts communications second among the fields marketing managers hold, at 88,800 people, and the median there is $166,790. It is the best-evidenced high-paying exit from this degree family.

⚠ If public relations is the aim, take the measurement courses. PR's weakest point professionally is proving it worked; the practitioners who can are the ones who move up.

⚠⚠ Check what your PR introduction actually covers. PUR3000 is the general profession at UF and FGCU and public affairs at UWF, and the difference is PR history, media relations and campaigns.

And build clips from week one, whatever the destination. Nothing in this family is licensed, so what you can show is the credential — and a student newspaper, a campus radio station or a nonprofit's social media are all available before anyone will pay you.

programs.note: The family — 14 Florida public institutions across five codes. ⚠ Journalism is 292 bachelor's at 5 institutions; communication, PR and advertising together are roughly 2,350. ⚠⚠ Read its degrees note on the JOU1100/JOU2100 and ADV3300/ADV4300 numbering splits.

⚠⚠⚠ The best-evidenced high-paying exit from this degree family, and almost nobody points at it. Census microdata puts COMMUNICATIONS second among the undergraduate fields held by marketing managers, at 88,800 people — and the marketing manager median is $166,790 against a PR specialist's $74,750.

⚠⚠ A genuine overlap rather than a neighbour: Digital Communication and Media (09.0702) is 29 Florida institutions and 797 credentials, filed in the communication family and doing design work. ⚠ If the visual side is the draw, that is where it lives.

⚠ A growing destination where this one is shrinking: training and development specialists number 452,300 with 43,900 annual openings against journalism's 3,400, and the field screens on a portfolio while valuing exactly the explanatory writing journalism teaches.

⚠ Corporate communication, internal communication and investor relations are business functions, and a communication degree with business coursework reaches them. ⚠⚠ The portable option if media contraction continues.

⚠ Named for a specific route: health communication is a named content area in the CHES credential, county health departments employ communication specialists, and CHES is coursework-based rather than major-based — so a communication graduate who planned 25 credits can reach it.

courses.reason: ⚠ Journalistic Writing and Reporting — 8 Florida institutions (3 state colleges, 5 universities), the most widely carried journalism course in the state. Sourcing, structure and deadline writing, which is the durable skill in this whole family.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida also carries JOU1100 Basic Reporting at 7 institutions, ALL state colleges, with NO overlap. Same subject, two numbers. Send the syllabus on transfer.

courses.reason: Basic Reporting — 7 institutions, all state colleges. The lower-division entry, and the cheapest way into reporting training.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ No institution carries both this and JOU2100.

courses.reason: Advanced Reporting — 4 institutions (FAU, UF, USF, UWF). The upper-division reporting course, and where investigative technique is taught.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ This project found JOU3342's statewide prerequisite names JOU3101 AND RTV4301 — and UWF carries JOU3101 but not RTV4301 while UNF carries neither. The state describes a prerequisite chain that does not exist at the institutions teaching the course.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Principles of Public Relations — 9 Florida institutions, the most widely carried course in this family. The profession's history, ethics and process.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ A documented divergence: UF and FGCU teach the general introduction, but UWF teaches INTRODUCTION TO PUBLIC AFFAIRS — government and nonprofit policy communication. Public affairs is a subfield of PR, so a UWF student misses PR history, media relations and campaigns entirely. Read the description, not the title.

courses.reason: Public Relations Campaigns — 6 institutions. The capstone, and the piece of work that becomes a portfolio entry.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ UWF uses PUR4801 for its campaigns capstone while statewide PUR4801 is Public Relations CASES — a different subject. Check which yours is.

courses.reason: Public Relations Cases — 5 institutions (FAMU, UCF, UNF, USF, UWF). Case-method analysis of real campaigns and crises.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Documented misfiling: UWF runs its campaigns CAPSTONE on this number, which statewide is the cases course. The two are different subjects.

courses.reason: Crisis Communications — 4 institutions. ⚠ The specialism that most reliably distinguishes a PR practitioner professionally, and the one clients pay most for.
Publicity Writing — 5 institutions. The practical writing course on the PR side, and the closest analogue to reporting.
Principles of Advertising — 7 institutions, the widest advertising course in Florida.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ This project found ADV3008 classified as BUSINESS (52.0101) at FAU and COMMUNICATION (09.0101) at FIU — a documented cross-family CIP disagreement on one course.

courses.reason: Media Planning — 4 universities (FGCU, UNF, USF, UWF). Where advertising money actually gets allocated, and a genuinely quantitative course.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida carries the identical title as ADV4300 at 4 DIFFERENT universities with no overlap. Same course, two upper-division numbers — a transfer-matching problem rather than a credit one.

courses.reason: Advertising Campaigns — 5 institutions. The capstone on the advertising side, and another portfolio piece.
⚠ Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Named deliberately: PR's weakest professional point is proving an effect, data journalism is where reporting is growing, and both need this.
Principles of Marketing — 24 institutions, all state colleges. ⚠ Named because the marketing ladder is the best-evidenced high-paying exit from this degree family.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ A 2000-level course; if a baccalaureate follows, check whether your programme wants MAR3023.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. The foundation everything in this family rests on.
English Composition II — 37 institutions. Research and argument, which is what reporting and campaign rationale both are.
Fundamentals of Speech Communication — 16 institutions. Interviewing, pitching and presenting — three different registers of the same skill, all central here.
